judgement.notes: We called the FDA decision a coin flip; the evidence was skewed (9-3 AdCom against, a prior CRL for the same deficiency, an indication narrowed to rescue the filing). Passing avoided the loss but the skew argued for a bearish stance.
judgement.actual_driver: Nov 20: second Complete Response Letter for deramiocel (no substantial evidence of effectiveness) plus FDA allegations of data integrity violations; $7.59 -> $1.92 (-75%).
judgement.early_signs: July 2026 AdCom 9-3 against; July 2025 CRL citing the same deficiency; PDUFA extension only after narrowing the indication; +76% run-up into the decision (cause unverified).
judgement.look_for: PDUFA after a negative AdCom plus a prior CRL: assume the FDA leans to rejection and treat the event as skewed, not a coin flip; a run-up into it adds downside.

idea: Whey protein costs easing from June record; needs FY27 cost commentary (Nov 17)

judgement.notes: Re-rated for a different reason than ours: management did NOT confirm cost relief (FY27 protein inflation guided high single digits, proteins ~70% hedged). Stock rose on self-help margin repair (pricing, $100M+ supply-chain savings, lapping $37M inventory charges) and EBITDA guided back to growth from a crushed base. Report was Nov 18, not Nov 17.
judgement.actual_driver: Nov 18 FY26 Q4: sales +7% to $692.0M (beat); FY27 adj. EBITDA guided $310-350M vs $288.8M despite flat-to-down sales, via low double-digit shake price increases, >=$100M 3-yr supply-chain savings, ~400bp gross margin expansion and lapping ~$37M inventory charges; new CEO trades growth for margin. +24% on the day ($11.01 -> $13.66), $16.08 by Nov 27. Nov 16 7-Eleven distribution deal helped into the print.
judgement.early_signs: 52-week low $7.33 on Oct 1 (crushed multiple); already +20% from our flag into the print; 7-Eleven deal Nov 16; dated print with a new CEO. Whey relief was never the swing factor: Aug Q3 call already pointed to continued inflation and price actions.
judgement.look_for: Crushed multiple + dated print + new CEO: watch for EBITDA guided back to growth via self-help (pricing + savings) rather than waiting for input costs; check hedge cover before assuming spot commodity relief reaches the P&L.

idea: AI/miner rebound: wait for earnings/CPI/NVDA

judgement.notes: 'Wait for confirmation' was right: confirmation never came (unfunded capex gap, slipped ARR target) and even Nvidia's beat did not stop the slide. The bulk of the fall was sector-wide AI data-centre financing fear, so 'avoid' would have been better than 'wait'.

judgement.early_signs: Microsoft's late-October capex shortfall from delayed third-party capacity; Applied Digital saying ~800MW still needed financing; neocloud group -13% Oct 26 - Nov 2; The Information's Childress delay story the day before results.
judgement.look_for: Capex-heavy neoclouds/miners: hyperscaler 'delayed third-party capacity' comments, peers' unfunded-capex disclosures and bank-lending headlines turning sour = move from wait to avoid (or short).
